Are you sure you don't share the HttpMessageDecoder between Channels ?
Ok so you call "close" from an other thread then the io-worker right ?
Ok that explain it.. I will commit a fix shortly..

Great! Looking forward for fix.
Thank you very much.

Just to add more context here is why you see the problem.

If you call Channel.close() a downstream event will get fired. The event will then processed and finally close the channel. After the channel is closed it trigger an upstream event to notify about the closed channel. The problem is that this event will _NOT_ get executed in the IO-Thread and so its possible to see a race-condition. This need to get fixed as this is a "global" problem.

issue.title: Allow to submit a Runnable to be executed in the io-thread

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body: It would be nice to let the user submit a Runnable that get executed in the io-thread (in the next loop). This will also help us to workaround the problems in the Thread-Model. See #187 and #140 for the flaws there
